parole.significato: A title used in several states in central and south-eastern Europe between the 7th century and the 20th century.
parole.testo: From South Slavic (compare Serbo-Croatian bȃn), from Proto-Slavic *banъ; see there for more.

parole.significato: A tower, turret or steeple in Southeastern Europe erected during the period of Ottoman domination on the area.
parole.testo: From a South Slavic language, from Turkish kule, from Persian قله (qolle), from Arabic قُلَّة (qulla, “pinnacle, zenith”).

parole.significato: The custom of honoring a family patron saint, celebrated chiefly by the Serbs, but also by some Macedonians, Montenegri…
parole.testo: From South Slavic slava / слава (slava), literally "fame, glory". The word is also used in some Slavic languages to wish blessings to another person.
